tweet_summary: UK news-style account 'UNN' (114k followers) declares 'BREAKING NEWS 🔥🔥🔥' that Itamar Ben-Gvir has been killed in an Iranian missile strike on his home — and that Israeli media's 'car crash' framing is a cover-up. 1.42M impressions, 21k likes, 4.7k RTs, image of Ben-Gvir. Replies celebrate the alleged death.
why_note_decision: Clear death hoax. PolitiFact, Yahoo/AFP fact-check, EBU Spotlight, IBTimes UK, and The Jewish Chronicle all confirm Ben-Gvir is alive — he posted 'I'm alive' on X on March 10, 2026. The hoax was part of a pro-Iran disinfo wave that also targeted Netanyahu and David Barnea. With 1.42M impressions and celebratory replies a note IS needed. The original note's substance is correct; it was rated NOT_HELPFUL likely because (a) it leans on 'unconfirmed/no reliable sources' instead of citing Ben-Gvir's own 'I'm alive' post + a fact-checker, and (b) the 'A prior crash occurred in 2024' line muddies the message.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note (a) clearly states Ben-Gvir is alive — citing his own March 10, 2026 'I'm alive' post on X OR a recognized fact-check (PolitiFact, AFP/Yahoo, EBU Spotlight, The Jewish Chronicle), AND (b) frames the death claim as a known pro-Iran disinformation hoax that also targeted Netanyahu/Barnea. AVOID the original note's failure (rated notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded 19, OpinionSpeculation 14, MissingKeyPoints 14, SourcesMissingOrUnreliable 11): do NOT hedge with 'unconfirmed/no reliable sources report' (Ben-Gvir HAS personally confirmed he is alive — say so directly), do NOT cite the unrelated 2024 car crash (it muddies the message), and do NOT use vague 'active as of March 4' — use the 'I'm alive' post and a dedicated fact-check. FAIL any note that endorses the death claim or hedges on whether he's alive.
reference_note: Itamar Ben-Gvir is alive. He posted 'I'm alive' on X on March 10, 2026 after viral pro-Iran hoaxes claimed he was killed in an Iranian missile strike. PolitiFact, AFP and EBU Spotlight have debunked the rumor; the same wave also falsely targeted Netanyahu and Mossad chief David Barnea. https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2026/mar/11/tweets/Israel-Minister-Ben-Gvir-no-dead/ https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/fact-check-ben-gvir-not-231638807.html

original_unhelpful_note.text: Rumors of Itamar Ben-Gvir's death in an Iranian missile strike, misreported as a car crash, are unconfirmed. No reliable sources report his death or a 2026 crash. He was active as of March 4, 2026. A prior crash occurred in 2024.    https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/government-ministers-accuse-ag-of-harming-iran-war-effort-with-call-to-fire-ben-gvir  https://www.timesofisrael.com/nine-people-killed-in-iranian-missile-strike-on-residential-area-in-beit-shemesh  https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-minister-ben-gvir-slightly-hurt-car-accident-2024-04-26  https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itamar_Ben-Gvir
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Substantively correct (Ben-Gvir alive) but rated NOT_HELPFUL (42 ratings; dominant notHelpfulNoteNotNeeded 19, then OpinionSpeculation 14, MissingKeyPoints 14, SourcesMissingOrUnreliable 11). Hedging language ('unconfirmed/no reliable sources') reads as weak; the unrelated 2024 car-crash line muddies the message; no citation of Ben-Gvir's own 'I'm alive' post or a dedicated fact-check (PolitiFact/AFP) despite their existence.

fact_check.claim_verdict: False. Ben-Gvir is alive (posted 'I'm alive' March 10, 2026); part of a pro-Iran death-hoax wave debunked by PolitiFact/AFP/EBU.
fact_check.notes: Same hoax wave targeted Netanyahu, Iddo Netanyahu, and Mossad's David Barnea. Originating in pro-Iran/regime accounts.

importance.lens_rationale: 1.42M impressions on a categorical 'official killed in war' death claim; geopolitically volatile during active Iran-Israel hostilities — exactly the class of misinformation Community Notes should suppress quickly.
